messages:
customer-ops: Hey team — enterprise customer (acct: acme-corp) sees malformed JSON from streaming chat API. Parser fails with \"Unexpected end of JSON input\". They reported two sessions today. Attaching minimal curl and response fragment. request_id=req_0a1b2c
ana: Thanks — can you paste the exact curl and the raw bytes they received? Are they using SSE or plain chunked HTTP streaming?
ingest-bot: Log ingested for req_0a1b2c, proxied via prod-edge-03, trace=trace-9f3a
customer-ops: They used standard chunked transfer (no SSE). Curl they ran:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/chat?model=redwood-2 --data '{"stream":true,"json_mode":"structured"}'
```
And the last chunk they showed (raw):
```
...\n{"id":0,"role":"assistant","content":{"type":"array","items":[{"intent":"ok","text":"Here is the summary"}]}}
{"id":1,"role":"assistant","content":{"type":"array","items":[{"intent":"next","text":"Follow-up"}]}
```
Note the second object is missing the final `}` for the outermost object (it ends after the items array). Parser fails.
ana: Got it. Two quick hypotheses: (A) upstream or proxy closed connection mid-chunk (FIN) or reset, truncating trailing bytes; (B) buffer/windowing caused chunk boundaries to split JSON in a way their parser doesn't tolerate. Which edge are they on (hosted/dedicated/private)?
customer-ops: Hosted API. They hit it from a backend service behind a corporate proxy (they also said a corporate gateway that does TLS inspection). They can reproduce with a small script.
sre_jake: Please ask the customer to run a raw TCP capture or curl with `--raw` to see exact bytes. Also check if their corporate proxy has an idle/read timeout ~60s. If our server emits final chunk after a pause, the proxy might tear down the connection mid-stream.
eng-marco: Another mitigation: include an explicit JSON envelope with length-prefix or a sentinel event at the end so customers can detect incomplete payloads. But we should still fix root cause. Could be NGINX upstream_read_timeout on our edge or cloud LB closing on keepalive.
ana: Customer, can you repro with `curl -v --no-buffer` and share headers? Example we asked them to run:
```
curl -v --no-buffer \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  --data '{"stream":true,"json_mode":"structured"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/chat?model=redwood-2
```
Also include the `Date` response header and `Transfer-Encoding` value.
customer-ops: Ran it, attached snippet. Response headers include `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, `Connection: keep-alive`, Date: Tue, 12 Apr 2032 16:22:10 GMT. The last server chunk size was 0x2a but then a reset on socket. They captured `RST, FIN` from remote.
ana: That points to upstream reset. eng-marco, can we grep edge logs for req_0a1b2c and look for an upstream disconnect / keepalive timeout around 16:22:10?
eng-marco: Looking. I see prod-edge-03 proxied to runner-gpu-12, and there was a 502 from runner-gpu-12 at 16:22:10 with TCP RST from that host. stacktrace shows runtime worker hit OOM during KV cache compaction and process restarted, causing socket RST. OOM could explain abrupt close.
sre_jake: OOM on runtime is important. That would drop connection mid-chunk. We should mark this as P1 for reliability and alert infra. For the customer: recommend retry with idempotent stream resume or add validation on client to handle truncated JSON (e.g., drop last partial object then request a follow-up message). Also propose server-side: emit final sentinel before closing.
ana: Customer update: they can reproduce with a reproducible script. They're blocked in production because their JSON parser throws and they don't have clean retry.
eng-marco: Short-term workaround we can push: add a final \"status\":\"complete\" event as soon as payload is generated and before any background compaction runs. I'll open an emergency PR to ensure the emitter flushes final chunk then yields to background work.
customer-ops: Customer is ok with temporary mitigation, wants ETA. Any chance to provide timeline?
ana: We'll target a hotfix rollout to prod-edge tomorrow (24hr). I'll file the incident and notify the customer. :thumbsup:
ingest-bot: Incident created INC-2026-042 for req_0a1b2c, severity=high, owner=eng-marco
sre_jake: Postmortem action items: (1) increase memory guardrail for runner-gpu processes; (2) ensure graceful shutdown waits for active stream flush; (3) add monitoring for midstream RST rate.
customer-ops: Thanks. I'll update the customer and request they implement a client-side defensive parser that tolerates a trailing partial object and retries the prompt if incomplete.
ana: Thanks all — triage complete, following up with timeline and PR link.
eng-marco: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/412 — adds explicit final sentinel and guards against compaction during active streams. Will pipeline to canary tonight.
customer-ops: Appreciated. Customer will test canary tomorrow and report.
